Change c0335. Location: 1818 Vol. III, Ch. I; 1831 Ch. XVIII.

Context before (unchanged): I found that I could not compose a female without again devoting several months to profound study and laborious disquisition.

1818 text: I had heard of some discoveries having been made by an English philosopher, the knowledge of which was material to my success, and I sometimes thought of obtaining my father's consent to visit England for this purpose; but I clung to every pretence of delay, and could not resolve to interrupt my returning tranquillity. My health, which had hitherto declined, was now much restored; and my spirits, when unchecked by the memory of my unhappy promise, rose proportionably.

1831 text: I had heard of some discoveries having been made by an English philosopher, the knowledge of which was material to my success, and I sometimes thought of obtaining my father's consent to visit England for this purpose; but I clung to every pretence of delay, and shrunk from taking the first step in an undertaking whose immediate necessity began to appear less absolute to me. A change indeed had taken place in me: my health, which had hitherto declined, was now much restored; and my spirits, when unchecked by the memory of my unhappy promise, rose proportionably.

Diff: I had heard of some discoveries having been made by an English philosopher, the knowledge of which was material to my success, and I sometimes thought of obtaining my father's consent to visit England for this purpose; but I clung to every pretence of delay, and [-could not resolve-] {+shrunk from taking the first step in an undertaking whose immediate necessity began+} to [-interrupt my returning tranquillity-] {+appear less absolute to me+} . [-My-] {+A change indeed had taken place in me: my+} health, which had hitherto declined, was now much restored; and my spirits, when unchecked by the memory of my unhappy promise, rose proportionably.

Context after (unchanged): My father saw this change with pleasure, and he turned his thoughts towards the best method of eradicating the remains of my melancholy, which every now and then would return by fits, and with a devouring blackness overcast the approaching sunshine.

result.rationale: Victor's resolve is recast: 'could not resolve to interrupt my returning tranquillity' becomes 'shrunk from taking the first step', making him a shirker whose urgency has faded, a shift in his motives and self-presentation of guilt and inaction.
